$ fleet queue fail 19479 --worker repo-worker-code --lane code-a --error "packet payload fails validation on retry" --reason-class deterministic
{"id": 19479, "status": "failed", "last_error": "packet payload fails validation on retry", "result": {"reason_class": "deterministic"}}

fleet queue complete

usage: repo-queue complete <task-id> [--worker <id>] [--lane <id>] [--result <json>] [--result-file <f>] [--telemetry <json>] [--execution <id>] [--queue <name>]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<task-id> (positional)task idrequiredThe claimed task to complete.
--workerworker idrepo-worker-codeHolder identity.
--lanelane idenv REPO_QUEUE_LANE, else nullHolder lane check.
--resultJSON object{} when neither result flag is givenThe completion result object. Must parse as a JSON object (non-JSON or non-object → exit 2).
--result-filefile pathunsetFile containing the result object. When both are given, --result-file is read after and wins over --result.
--telemetryJSON objectunsetTelemetry whose keys must be a subset of the four fields pool, model, effort, cost_usd — unknown fields die exit 2 listing the allowed set. Values are merged into the result only for fields the result doesn’t already carry.
--executionexecution idunsetFolded into result.execution = {lane, session_id, fallback: bool, fallback_reason?, assigned?} when the result doesn’t already carry an execution key, and also sent as the body’s execution.
--queuequeue nameparsed, never usedDead flag — see discrepancy note.

Behaviour. Terminal done, via POST /complete on the fallback-switch path (a primary-store failure switches, exit 6). Output: row or {task, lane_ledger[, follow_on_task_id]} — a triage completion can spawn a follow-on task whose id rides the envelope. Completion closes the timeline binding window.

Client-side completion dressing (all fail-soft, explicit caller values win):

  • result.dominant_model: the bound session’s dominant serving model over the task’s claim window (route_attempt call count), when derivable.
  • Telemetry defaulting: pool/model/effort are filled from the claim stamp, else the completing session’s serving leaf / declared route pool; cost_usd stays null (no cost readout is sourceable). effort is recorded only from resolved session messages, never inferred from route names. A claim stamp written through the route provider (opencode-route) names the route id in claim_model — that is the pool, not a serving leaf — so it never supplies model; the session’s serving leaf, or null, does.

The evidence gate. Shape validation alone used to let a fix-class row complete done on any non-empty evidence string while its issue was open and a draft PR still carried the work. Now, a completion that requires a disposition must carry result.disposition — the verified readback record produced by verify-disposition (next section):

{ "checked_at": "…", "source": "…", "issue": { "number": 0, "state": "…", "state_reason": "…", "closed_at": "…", "closed_by": "…" }, "pulls": [{ "number": 0, "state": "…", "is_draft": false, "merged_at": "…" }], "verdict": "…", "follow_up": "…" }

The gate is pure (no network): it parses the record, checks freshness (≤ 1800 s old by default; >300 s in the future is unreadable clock skew), checks it describes the task’s issue, checks the verdict against the readback, checks every PR the completion result links (pr/pr_url/merged_pr fields) appears in the readback, and checks any follow-up. Every rejection leaves the task claimed and names the defect (“…; the task remains claimed”). The five verdicts and their per-verdict rules are specified under verify-disposition below.

Help: complete takes no --queue flag — an earlier dead --queue (parsed but never read by the source) was removed from the parser and the usage (#13174).

Exit codes: 0 completed · 1 disposition gate rejection (task remains claimed) · 2 usage / non-object result / unknown telemetry field · 3 transport · 4 broker store failure · 5 no matching claimed row · 6 fallback switch.

$ fleet queue verify-disposition 13165 --repo developing-today/code --json > /tmp/disp.json
$ fleet queue complete 19479 --worker repo-worker-code --lane code-a --result-file /tmp/disp-result.json
{"id": 19479, "status": "done", "completed_at": "2026-11-23T04:25:00Z"}

fleet queue verify-disposition

usage: repo-queue verify-disposition <issue> --repo <owner/name> [--pr <n,n>] [--follow-up-task <id> | --follow-up-issue <n|url> | --follow-up-pr <n>] [--reason <text>] [--staleness-seconds <n>] [--json]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<issue> (positional)issue numberrequiredThe issue to read back from GitHub.
--repoowner/namerequiredThe issue’s repo. Missing → exit 2.
--prcomma-separated PR numbersunsetExplicitly linked PRs to include in the readback.
--follow-up-tasktask idunsetFollow-up target: a queue task (checked by the broker at completion — only the queue knows if it is live). Mutually exclusive with the other follow-up flags.
--follow-up-issueissue number or URLunsetFollow-up target: a same-repo issue; its own readback (state + explicit links) is embedded.
--follow-up-prPR numberunsetFollow-up target: a successor PR.
--reasontextrequired when any follow-up target is givenWhy the follow-up owns the remainder. Any follow-up target without --reason → exit 2.
--staleness-secondsinteger seconds1800 (30 min)Freshness window for the record; must be positive (exit 2 otherwise).
--jsonbooleanoffPrint the raw record object. Without it, a human summary.

Behaviour. Reads the issue and its linked PRs back from GitHub, live (never from a remembered claim) and prints the disposition a terminal completion must carry. Readback assembly: gh api repos/<repo>/issues/<n> (the REST form, because it carries closed_by); gh pr list --state all --limit 300 --json number,state,isDraft,mergedAt,body; a search union ("<issue> in:body", limit 100) because the 300 newest PRs are not the whole history; then an individual gh pr view for any explicitly linked/successor PR the union lacks. A PR counts as linked when it is named by queue provenance / --pr, or its body carries an explicit marker — Refs #n, Fixes #n, Related program: #n. A bare prose #n is not a link (except that the Related program: prose marker is honored — it is the only link the draft PR in the motivating case had to its issue).

Either way (--json or human summary) the verb then runs the offline gate on its own record: exit 0 when the record would pass, exit 1 when the broker’s gate would reject it, and exit 1 when the issue or PR list cannot be read from GitHub at all. Usage errors exit 2.

The five verdicts (exactly five; derivation and gate rules):

VerdictDerived whenGate requires
merged_verifiedsome pull in the readback is merged≥1 merged pull in the readback
closed_verifiedissue closed and no unfinished pullsissue state actually closed (a close timestamp on an open issue is a superseded close, not evidence)
open_draft_with_followupunfinished pulls exist, nothing merged, issue not cleanly closeda recorded follow_up; while the issue is OPEN, unfinished pulls are allowed only under this or the next verdict, with the follow-up on record
open_draft_superseded(operator-asserted; same derivation family)a recorded follow_up
invalid_no_worknone of the above (no merged pull, issue open, no unfinished pull)rejected if any linked pull still carries work

A pull is unfinished when it is not merged (merged_at null) and not closed.

Follow-up checks: reason required; target must be one of task_id, issue_url, successor_pr. A follow-up issue must not be the issue being completed, must be open, must link the completed issue with an explicit marker, and must link every unfinished PR. A successor PR must be in the readback and must be merged. A task target is checked broker-side: the task must exist, not be the completing task, be in a live (non-terminal) status, and name the same issue.

Intentional-close exception: a closed issue may leave related work open only when the close was a deliberate act by a person (the readback’s closed_by is checked against automation) and a verified follow-up owns the remainder.

Exit codes: 0 record would pass the gate · 1 gate would reject it, or GitHub readback unreadable · 2 usage (including missing --repo, follow-up without --reason, non-positive --staleness-seconds).

$ fleet queue verify-disposition 13165 --repo developing-today/code --json
{"checked_at": "2026-11-23T04:24:00Z", "source": "github-readback", "issue": {"number": 13165, "state": "open", "state_reason": null, "closed_at": null, "closed_by": null}, "pulls": [], "verdict": "invalid_no_work", "follow_up": null}
(exit 1 — no merged pull and no follow-up on record; a completion carrying this record would be rejected)

fleet queue reprioritize

usage: repo-queue reprioritize <task-id> <new-priority> [--reason <text>] [--worker <id>]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<task-id> (positional)task idrequiredThe queued task whose priority changes.
<new-priority> (positional)priority valuerequiredA number, or a category name the validator maps to one (validate::resolve_priority). Missing or unresolvable → exit 2.
--reasontextunsetWhy the priority changed; recorded with the change.
--workerworker idthe authenticated caller identityThe acting worker. The actor is the authenticated caller identity presented over the broker’s token channel; no free-form actor string is accepted.

Behaviour. Calls the broker’s POST /reprioritize; the broker applies the new priority in the Turso queue store and syncs the task’s GitHub category to match. Prints the served task row as JSON. Landed in #14100 (PR #14203) and listed in the queue domain’s registry subcommand inventory, so fleet queue --help shows it.

Exit codes: 0 success · 2 usage (including a missing or unresolvable priority).

fleet queue: the fallback queue

The fallback queue is the GitHub-issue-comment queue: the queue used when the primary broker/store is down — and, via the permanent fallback switch, whenever a work verb’s primary call fails. All state lives in issue comments; there is no database and nothing to reconcile when the backend returns — the broker system re-derives queue state from labels and its own tables as it already does after any drift.

Group usage:

usage: repo-queue fallback <scan|status|claim|heartbeat|release|complete|unblock> ...
  • Work items are open issues carrying the fleet’s existing labels queue/queued (waiting), queue/claimed (held), queue/blocked (blocked) — the same labels the broker-backed system maintains; no parallel taxonomy. Blocked items sit outside the scan sweep and cannot be claimed.
  • Repos: the sweep covers five, in pilot order — developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber, dezren39/darwin-nix, dezren39/fleet. Shortcuts: code, opencode, openchamber, nix, fleet. Full names are developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber, dezren39/darwin-nix, dezren39/fleet.
  • Worker identity: every fleet worker posts to GitHub as the same account, so comment authorship cannot tell workers apart — the marker’s worker id is the only identity the lease can be keyed on. Therefore --worker is required, never defaulted (or env FLEET_FALLBACK_WORKER); ids must match [A-Za-z0-9._-], max 64 chars. Plain (unmarked) comments do NOT renew a claim.
  • Exit codes mirror the primary client (see core verbs): 0 ok, 2 usage, 3 the GitHub transport itself failed (gh missing/erroring), 5 the verb ran but the claim state forbids the action, 1 a complete whose disposition the gate rejected or whose record could not be read.
  • All fallback verbs print JSON except where noted; every verb’s JSON carries "mode": "fallback" on scan/status.

Sources: fallback.rs, client transport, disposition.rs.

The marker grammar

The claim is the first line of a comment, exactly (the fleet-claim v1 grammar):

<!-- fleet-claim v1 kind=claim worker=<id> ts=<rfc3339-utc> -->
<!-- fleet-claim v1 kind=heartbeat worker=<id> ts=<rfc3339-utc> -->
<!-- fleet-claim v1 kind=release worker=<id> outcome=<done|free> ts=<rfc3339-utc> -->
<!-- fleet-claim v1 kind=unblock worker=<id> ts=<rfc3339-utc> -->

A human-readable line sits under the marker. The marker’s embedded ts is authoritative. Marker reads paginate comments at 100/page, max 10 pages; a read that ends on a full 10th page errors rather than returning a truncated marker set.

The lease and the claim-state fold

The lease: a claim stays live while the holder posts heartbeat markers. Default window 30 minutes, overridable per-verb with --lease-min or globally with env FLEET_QUEUE_FALLBACK_LEASE_MIN. (30, not 20: worker checkpoints land at most ~15 min apart and the fix timebox is 45 min, so a 20-minute lease would let a live claim look dead between checkpoints.)

Claim state fold (a fold over the issue’s marker events in comment order):

  • free — no claim events. Claimable.
  • released {worker, outcome, ts} — the holder released. Claimable.
  • live {worker, last_activity, age_seconds} — last marker inside the lease. Not claimable by others.
  • stale {…} — older than the lease; any worker may claim, superseding. Claimable.
  • contested {holder, challenger, ts} — a claim posted while another’s claim is live contests the issue: hands-off for everyone while the contest is younger than the lease. A contest ages out once every challenger has been silent a full lease window (a repeat claim refreshes that challenger’s contest); a release from a challenger clears their contest at once. The holder may heartbeat throughout. Not claimable.

Claimable = free | released | stale.

The permanent fallback switch (exit 6)

The GitHub fallback is not an outage-only mode anymore. For the work verbs — claim, heartbeat, checkpoint, complete, health — any primary-store failure (broker unreachable, or an {ok:false} envelope from the broker) switches the caller to the GitHub fallback for that work instead of dying:

  • stderr: repo-queue: primary queue store failed on <verb> (exit <n>): <err>; switching this work to the GitHub fallback
  • stdout: one JSON object {"ok": false, "fallback": true, "switch_to": "github-fallback", "verb": <verb>, "mode_line": {"verb": …, "mode": "db-degraded", "route": "github-markers"}, "broker_exit": <n>, "error": <err>, "hint": "continue this work with: fleet queue fallback scan|claim|heartbeat|release|unblock"}
  • exit 6, so a worker loop can branch on it without parsing prose.
  • Escape hatch: env REPO_QUEUE_NO_FALLBACK_SWITCH=1 restores plain die-on-error.

The primary claim path also guards in the other direction — the no-double-serve guard: after a successful primary claim, if the issue is live or contested in the fallback under a different worker, the primary task is blocked back with reason-class fallback_held and the claim answers exit 5 (see core verbs).

fleet queue fallback scan

usage: repo-queue fallback scan [--repo <repo>] [--limit <1..100>] [--lease-min <minutes>]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
--reporepo or shortcutall five sweep reposRestrict the sweep to one repo (shortcut names resolve: code, opencode, openchamber, nix, fleet).
--limitinteger15Max items; range 1..=100 (outside → usage error).
--lease-mininteger minutes30 (or env FLEET_QUEUE_FALLBACK_LEASE_MIN)Lease window used to fold claim states.
(positionals)—none acceptedscan takes no positional arguments — see discrepancy note.

Behaviour. Sweeps the fallback repos’ labelled issues (queue/queued, queue/claimed, queue/blocked) and folds each issue’s claim state. Output JSON: {"mode":"fallback", "generated_at", "lease_seconds", "items": [{"repo","number","title","url","labels","blocked","claim": <state JSON>}], "summary": {"total", "claimable"}, "notes": […]}. Items are ranked claimable first (free/released/stale), then live, then contested/blocked; a blocked item never ranks claimable even if its marker fold reads free — the label is the block. Per-issue comment-read failures land in notes and the issue is folded with no markers rather than failing the sweep.

Help: the group usage line lists scan [--repo <repo>] [--limit <1..100>] [--lease-min <minutes>] — fallback scan takes no positionals at all (they are a usage error); its repo filter is the --repo flag. The top-level usage lists the full fallback subcommand set, complete included. This chapter documents the implementation behaviour.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage (including positionals, out-of-range --limit) · 3 GitHub transport failed.

$ fleet queue fallback scan --repo code --limit 5
{"mode": "fallback", "generated_at": "2026-11-23T04:30:00Z", "lease_seconds": 1800, "items": [{"repo": "developing-today/code", "number": 13165, "title": "Write the fleet book", "url": "https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13165", "labels": ["queue/queued"], "blocked": false, "claim": {"state": "free", "claimable": true}}], "summary": {"total": 1, "claimable": 1}, "notes": []}

Output JSON: {"mode":"fallback", "repo", "number", "url", "lease_seconds", "blocked": bool, "last_unblock": {"worker","ts"}|null, "claim": <state JSON>} where state JSON is one of {"state":"free","claimable":true}, {"state":"released","claimable":true,"worker","outcome","released_at"}, {"state":"live"|"stale","claimable":bool,"worker","last_activity","age_seconds"}, {"state":"contested","claimable":false,"worker"(holder),"challenger","contested_at"}.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 GitHub transport failed.

$ fleet queue fallback status code 13165
{"mode": "fallback", "repo": "developing-today/code", "number": 13165, "url": "https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13165", "lease_seconds": 1800, "blocked": false, "last_unblock": null, "claim": {"state": "live", "claimable": false, "worker": "repo-worker-code", "last_activity": "2026-11-23T04:28:00Z", "age_seconds": 120}}

fleet queue fallback claim

usage: repo-queue fallback claim <repo> <issue-number> --worker <id> [--lease-min <minutes>] [--note <text>]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<repo> (positional)repo or shortcutrequiredThe issue’s repo.
<issue-number> (positional)integerrequiredThe issue number.
--workerworker idrequired (or env FLEET_FALLBACK_WORKER)Claiming worker identity — the marker’s worker id is the lease key. Must match [A-Za-z0-9._-], max 64 chars. Never defaulted.
--lease-mininteger minutes30 (or env FLEET_QUEUE_FALLBACK_LEASE_MIN)Lease window.
--notetextunsetHuman-readable note placed under the claim marker.

Behaviour. Refuses (exit 5) when the issue is blocked (label), closed, or under a live/contested claim by another worker. Otherwise posts the claim marker comment (“Picked up by <worker> — working this now. … after <lease> minutes of silence any other worker may pick this up.”), then re-reads the markers: races are detected on read-back (if the fold now shows a contest or another holder, the claim did not take). On success it sets labels queue/claimed + work/assigned, removing queue/queued.

No-double-serve note: this is the fallback side of the guard described in core verbs — a fallback claim on an issue the primary queue currently holds does not merge the two claims; workers must resolve the contest through the fold (the primary claim path blocks its own task back when it detects a live fallback hold by a different worker).

Exit codes: 0 claimed · 2 usage / missing or malformed --worker · 3 GitHub transport failed · 5 issue blocked, closed, or live/contested under another worker; or the read-back shows the claim did not take.

$ fleet queue fallback claim code 13165 --worker repo-worker-code
{"mode": "fallback", "repo": "developing-today/code", "number": 13165, "claim": {"state": "live", "claimable": false, "worker": "repo-worker-code", "last_activity": "2026-11-23T04:30:00Z", "age_seconds": 0}}

fleet queue fallback heartbeat

usage: repo-queue fallback heartbeat <repo> <issue-number> --worker <id> [--lease-min <minutes>] [--note <text>]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<repo> (positional)repo or shortcutrequiredThe issue’s repo.
<issue-number> (positional)integerrequiredThe issue number.
--workerworker idrequired (or env FLEET_FALLBACK_WORKER)Holder identity. Never defaulted.
--lease-mininteger minutes30 (or env FLEET_QUEUE_FALLBACK_LEASE_MIN)Lease window the renewed claim is folded under.
--notetextunsetHuman-readable progress note under the heartbeat marker.

Behaviour. Posts a heartbeat marker, renewing your lease. Only the current holder’s markers renew; heartbeating someone else’s live claim does not take it over (the fold keeps the holder; your marker at most contests if it were a claim — a heartbeat is not).

Exit codes: 0 heartbeat posted · 2 usage / missing or malformed --worker · 3 GitHub transport failed · 5 the claim state forbids the action.

$ fleet queue fallback heartbeat code 13165 --worker repo-worker-code --note "chapters 2 of 6 drafted"
{"mode": "fallback", "repo": "developing-today/code", "number": 13165, "claim": {"state": "live", "claimable": false, "worker": "repo-worker-code", "last_activity": "2026-11-23T04:45:00Z", "age_seconds": 0}}

fleet queue fallback release

usage: repo-queue fallback release <repo> <issue-number> --worker <id> [--lease-min <minutes>] [--outcome done|free] [--summary <text>]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<repo> (positional)repo or shortcutrequiredThe issue’s repo.
<issue-number> (positional)integerrequiredThe issue number.
--workerworker idrequired (or env FLEET_FALLBACK_WORKER)Holder identity. Never defaulted.
--lease-mininteger minutes30 (or env FLEET_QUEUE_FALLBACK_LEASE_MIN)Lease window.
--outcomedone|freeunsetdone keeps the terminal state; free hands the work back unworked.
--summarytextunsetHuman-readable summary under the release marker.

Behaviour. Posts a release marker with the outcome. done keeps the terminal state (labels: queue/claimed/work/assigned removed, nothing restored); free hands the work back unworked and restores queue/queued. Plain release --outcome done remains the way to hand back work that carries no disposition (contrast complete below). A release from a challenger clears their contest at once.

Exit codes: 0 released · 2 usage / missing or malformed --worker / bad --outcome · 3 GitHub transport failed · 5 the claim state forbids the action.

$ fleet queue fallback release code 13165 --worker repo-worker-code --outcome free --summary "cannot take this now; back to the pool"
{"mode": "fallback", "repo": "developing-today/code", "number": 13165, "claim": {"state": "released", "claimable": true, "worker": "repo-worker-code", "outcome": "free", "released_at": "2026-11-23T04:50:00Z"}}

fleet queue fallback complete

usage: repo-queue fallback complete <repo> <issue-number> --worker <id> --summary <text> --result <path> [--pr <n[,n...]>] [--lease-min <minutes>]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<repo> (positional)repo or shortcutrequiredThe issue’s repo.
<issue-number> (positional)integerrequiredThe issue number.
--workerworker idrequired (or env FLEET_FALLBACK_WORKER)Holder identity. Never defaulted.
--summarytextrequiredCompletion summary posted with the release-done marker.
--resultfile pathrequiredA disposition record file — the output of fleet queue verify-disposition <issue> --repo <repo> --json (see lifecycle verbs).
--prcomma-separated PR numbersunsetThe completion’s linked PRs, for the gate’s coverage check.
--lease-mininteger minutes30 (or env FLEET_QUEUE_FALLBACK_LEASE_MIN)Lease window.

Behaviour — offline gate parity. Broker parity: --result must pass the broker’s offline disposition gate (disposition::check — the same pure gate the broker applies, including the 1800 s freshness rule and the five-verdict rules in lifecycle verbs) for this issue before anything is posted; a rejection posts nothing, the claim stays live, and the verb exits 1.

On a pass it posts the release-done marker with the summary and the full record in a ```fleet-disposition fenced block, so the record stays consumable from the marker stream when the broker returns.

UNCHECKED follow-ups. The one broker-only check — a follow_up’s task_id against the live queue — cannot run from a fallback seat: such a record is completed with that check flagged UNCHECKED in the comment and the verb output, never silently treated as checked.

Exit codes: 0 completed · 1 disposition gate rejection or unreadable record (nothing posted; claim stays live) · 2 usage / missing required flag / malformed --worker · 3 GitHub transport failed · 5 the claim state forbids the action.

$ fleet queue verify-disposition 13165 --repo developing-today/code --json > /tmp/disp.json
$ fleet queue fallback complete code 13165 --worker repo-worker-code --summary "Book chapters merged" --result /tmp/disp.json
{"mode": "fallback", "repo": "developing-today/code", "number": 13165, "completed": true, "verdict": "merged_verified", "follow_up_task_check": "n/a"}

<repo> (positional)repo or shortcutrequiredThe issue’s repo.
<issue-number> (positional)integerrequiredThe issue number.
--workerworker idrequired (or env FLEET_FALLBACK_WORKER)Overriding worker identity — the override is worker-scoped and recorded. Never defaulted.
--reasontextrequiredWhy the block is overridden; recorded in the unblock marker. Missing → exit 2.

The fallback form of the broker’s manual override: posts an unblock marker recording the override + reason, clears the queue/blocked label and restores queue/queued, then verifies the label transition landed. Refusals (exit 5): an issue that is closed, not blocked, or under a live or contested claim.

{"mode": "fallback", "repo": "developing-today/code", "number": 13165, "blocked": false, "last_unblock": {"worker": "repo-worker-code", "ts": "2026-11-23T04:55:00Z"}, "claim": {"state": "free", "claimable": true}}

fleet queue: dispatch and sessions

dispatch, session, and surfaces are not broker verbs: they are the absorbed fleet-place reference implementation, deciding where a build job runs across the fleet’s GitHub Actions copies and runner providers, and dispatching it there as the developing-today GitHub App. The surface registry is data (fleet-surfaces.json); no surface is hardcoded. Errors in this family print repo-queue: <msg> and exit 2. This dispatch is unrelated to fleet dispatch / dispatch-test at the top level of the binary (separate domains).

Shared context is in fleet queue: core verbs.

Sources: placement.rs, fleet-surfaces.json.

fleet queue dispatch

usage: repo-queue dispatch --repo <owner/name> --command '<cmd>' [--ref REF] [--runner auto|github|blacksmith] [--platform linux|macos] [--container IMAGE] [--surface ID] [--followup HANDLE|OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID] [--push-nix-cache] [--actions-cache KEY:PATH] [--actions-cache-restore-key PREFIX]... [--allow-paid-blacksmith MINUTES] [--laptop-busy] [--dispatch] [--json] [--registry PATH]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
--repoowner/namerequiredTarget repo; must match a surface’s targets. Missing → exit 2.
--commandcommand stringrequiredThe command the surface’s fleet-command.yml workflow runs. Missing → exit 2.
--refgit refempty (workflow default)Git ref to run at.
--runnerauto|github|blacksmithautoProvider preference; other values die exit 2.
--platformlinux|macoslinuxOther values die exit 2. An undocumented alias --macos exists in source.
--containerimage nameunsetContainer image for surfaces with container_input; empty value dies exit 2.
--surfacesurface idunsetPin one surface; an unknown id dies (--surface <id>: no such surface in the registry), exit 2.
--followupHANDLE or OWNER/REPO#RUN_IDunsetChain this dispatch after a previous run (portable run reference).
--push-nix-cachebooleanoffAsk the workflow to push the Nix cache (needs the surface’s cache secrets).
--actions-cacheKEY:PATHunsetOne Actions cache binding; must be non-empty KEY:PATH, else exit 2. (Single value in source despite the plural name.)
--actions-cache-restore-keyprefixunsetRestore-key prefixes. Repeatable.
--allow-paid-blacksmithminutes (number)0Raise the Blacksmith paid cap for this dispatch only; must parse as a number, else exit 2.
--laptop-busybooleanoffManually mark the laptop busy (the registry’s saturation signal for the codespace tier is deliberately a manual flag, “not scraped telemetry”).
--dispatchbooleanoffActually dispatch. Without it the verb is a dry run (the default).
--jsonbooleanoffMachine-readable decision/session output.
--registryfile pathresolution order (see surfaces)Placement registry file.
--assume-owner-loadowner=N[,owner=N…]unsetTesting override, labeled as simulation in the output: pretend owner load.
--assume-blacksmith-usedminutesunsetTesting override, labeled as simulation in the output: pretend Blacksmith minutes already used.

Behaviour. Loads the registry, computes live capacity per surface (owner concurrency caps, macOS caps, Blacksmith free-minute budget, codespace liveness, local session history/stickiness), picks a surface + provider, and prints the placement decision. Dry-run is the default: without --dispatch nothing is dispatched. With --dispatch it workflow-dispatches fleet-command.yml on the chosen surface’s repo (as the GitHub App installation token when the registry says dispatch_as app, else the signed-in user’s token), writes a session record, and prints its handle: fp_ + 128-bit random.

Known discrepancy: the help line says [--ref REF]; the placement module’s frozen-v1 interface comment says [--ref SHA]. Cosmetic only; the flag itself is identical. This chapter documents --ref REF.

Exit codes: 0 decision printed (dry run) or dispatched · 2 usage / unknown surface / bad flag value (this family’s errors are exit 2).

$ fleet queue dispatch --repo developing-today/code --command 'nix build .#fleet' --json | jq -r .mode
dry-run (no session written; pass --dispatch to submit)
$ fleet queue dispatch --repo developing-today/code --command 'nix build .#fleet' --dispatch --json | jq -r .handle
fp_d0a842c9bd33aa2999f5a12393397ab9

fleet queue session status

usage: repo-queue session <status|result|list> [HANDLE|OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID] [--mine] [--json] [--registry PATH]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<handle> (positional)session handle fp_… or portable ref OWNER/REPO#RUN_IDrequiredThe session to inspect. A portable reference is resolved directly against GitHub without the local store.
--minebooleanoffAccepted on the session group (used by list; see below).
--jsonbooleanoffPrint the record as JSON instead of the one-line text form.
--registryfile pathresolution order (see surfaces)Placement registry file.

Behaviour. Dispatch commits the session locally, then mirrors it to the queue broker on a best-effort basis. For an fp_ handle, status selects the newer local or broker record by updated_at (the broker wins ties). A broker record can seed an empty local store on a second seat. Status then refreshes the provider state and prints the handle, state, surface and run URL. A failed mirror read leaves the local path available.

Help: a help flag after the subcommand prints the session usage and exits 0 — session status --help asks for help; it does not look up a session named --help (#13175). The flags documented here come from source.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage / no such handle / missing handle (session status needs a HANDLE).

$ fleet queue session status fp_d0a842c9bd33aa2999f5a12393397ab9
fp_d0a842c9bd33aa2999f5a12393397ab9: state=running surface="fleet-org" run=https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45146933211

fleet queue session list

usage: repo-queue session <status|result|list> [HANDLE|OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID] [--mine] [--json] [--registry PATH]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
--minebooleanoffFilter to records whose submitted_by is the current user.
--jsonbooleanoffPrint {"sessions": […]} instead of one status line per session.

Behaviour. Combines the local store with up to 200 broker records, deduplicates by handle and sorts by creation time, newest first. A failed broker read leaves the local records available. Listing shows the recorded state without polling GitHub. Text form is one status line per session, or no sessions; --json gives {"sessions": […]}. Group-level behaviour: session with no subcommand prints the usage and returns 2; session --help prints usage and returns 0; an unknown subcommand dies exit 2.

$ fleet queue session list
fp_d0a842c9bd33aa2999f5a12393397ab9: state=running surface="fleet-org" run=https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45146933211

fleet queue surfaces

usage: repo-queue surfaces [--json] [--registry PATH]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
--registryfile pathresolution order (see Behaviour)Registry file to print.

Behaviour. Prints the resolved placement registry as pretty JSON, exit 0. The optional --json flag selects the same output. surfaces --help prints a short usage instead of the registry. Registry resolution order: --registry <path> or env FLEET_PLACE_REGISTRY → a home copy → the source-tree relative path → the registry embedded in the binary. Registry shape (version 2): {comment, version, laptop: {busy, busy_source, note}, owners: {<owner>: {concurrent_jobs_cap, concurrent_macos_cap, plan, private_minutes_monthly}}, surfaces: […]}.

The shipped surfaces: fleet-personal (github-actions, dezren39/fleet, App installation, active), fleet-org (github-actions, developing-today/fleet, user-token dispatch, active; also the Blacksmith host), fleet-forks (github-actions, developing-today-forks/fleet, public targets only, active), org-run (standby, retained for manual use; placement prefers fleet-org), fleet-org-blacksmith (kind blacksmith, Linux-only fallback; budget 3000 free min/mo, paid cap 0 — paid overage disabled unless a dispatch explicitly supplies --allow-paid-blacksmith), codespace-overflow (kind codespace, status pending-scope, max 3 live, 180 core-hours/mo budget; uses existing codespaces only, never creates them), laptop (kind laptop, handoff-only — a placement record only; this adapter never runs shell commands on the laptop). Targets accept exact owner/repo, owner/*, or *. sticky_queue_threshold: 2 and selection_priority (10 for the active runners, 20 for org-run) drive the cascade.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage / unreadable registry.

fleet queue: inspection and admin

The inspection and admin verbs read the queue’s history and operate its side systems: timeline / history (one task’s event timeline), signal (the wake-up signal file), models (serving-model rollup), outbox (the creation outbox for GitHub objects), and stack (merge-intent stacks).

Shared context — the global exit-code vocabulary (0 ok, 1 gate/not-found, 2 usage, 3 transport/401, 4 broker store failure, 5 no-claim/no-row, 6 fallback switch) — is stated in fleet queue: core verbs.

Sources: commands_query.rs, commands_lifecycle.rs, fallback_stack.rs, creation_outbox.rs, merge_intent.rs.

fleet queue timeline

usage: repo-queue timeline <task-id> [--worker <id>] [--json]
FlagArgumentDefaultMeaning
<task-id> (positional)task idrequiredThe task whose timeline to render.
--workerworker idrepo-worker-codeAttribution; the events queries don’t use it beyond the shared envelope.
--jsonbooleanoffPrint {"task_id": n, "events": […], "served": […]} instead of the rendered timeline.

Behaviour. For each of 14 event kinds — claimed, session_bound, lane_session_bound, model_stamp, session_unbound, session_binding_cleared, completed, lease_expired, lease_expired_at_cap, claim_refused, released, parked, failed, cancelled — it calls /events-list {task_id, kind, limit:1000}, merges, sorts by event id, and collapses duplicates (same kind/session/leaf/trigger within 120 s = one record written by two surfaces). If the broker doesn’t serve /events-list, it prints the interim direct-DB SQL to stderr and exits 3. Output: a rendered timeline (binding windows with the exact resolved models per window, joined from the route ledger). With --json: {"task_id": n, "events": […], "served": [{"session_id", "start", "end", "segments": […]}]}; an empty timeline prints task <id>: no timeline records (or the empty JSON shape), exit 0.

Exit codes: 0 ok (including empty timeline) · 2 usage · 3 broker does not serve /events-list / transport · 4 broker store failure.

$ fleet queue timeline 19479
task 19479 timeline:
  claimed          2026-11-23T04:05:00Z  worker=repo-worker-code lane=code-a
  session_bound    2026-11-23T04:05:01Z  session=ses_01J9EXAMPLE0000000000000
  checkpoint       2026-11-23T04:20:00Z  stage=drafting
  served: ses_01J9EXAMPLE0000000000000 04:05:00Z–… (1 segment)
