Quota shadow and weekly review

AMD’s active PM aggregator state contained 64 shadow records with distinct timestamps and populated live and shadow orderings. The first retained record was at 02:30:06.420 UTC and the last was at 18:00:03.915 UTC. The largest interval between consecutive records was 1,068.112 seconds. Forty-one of the 64 records had different orderings. These are shadow comparisons. They do not establish which pool actually received a job or how the unselected pool would have performed. The collection spans less than one day of the S3 week. Record deployment provenance, continuity and S2 scoring before starting the gated S4 trial. At readback, the user timer for the gatherer was active and its 18:00 invocation had succeeded. S3 acceptance · Gatherer

The source defines the S7 weekly review as a persistent user timer on Monday at 07:20 local with up to 60 seconds of randomized delay. Both user and system managers on AMD reported LoadState=not-found for quota-weekly-review.timer during this observation. The published first report demonstrates report generation. Timer activation still needs its own deployment and firing receipt. Timer declaration · First report

Remote verification, fork convergence and releases

A dispatch receipt should identify the source tree under test, command, workflow revision, image digest, runner class and assertion. A green image build, a green export and a passing workload answer different questions. Keep each result when a later step fails. Remote build and test runbook

Which environment can prove the result?

The fleet-build investigation traced failures to differences between the image’s configured editor user and the root account used by the workflow. Recent upstream changes addressed Nix feature configuration, build users and the home directory used during pure evaluation. A subsequent root smoke check encountered a checkout owned by the earlier user. The correction made the smoke checkout root-owned before the root check. The branch run at 2db5a5d8 passed all eight jobs. Main’s subsequent publication workflow on merge commit 95d6c5da succeeded in run 45228189518. A runner pulling the published digest and a consumer command succeeding still need their own receipts. The container investigation remains subject to the recorded item-specific hold. Container investigation · Upstream image correction · Smoke correction · Eight-job branch run · Main publication

Proposed verification legPlacement and oracle
Build and pull the imageRecord source tree, platform, registry manifest digest and actual runner digest. Refuse a successful-build claim when upload or pull failed.
Run the workflow’s supported toolchainUnder its actual UID and HOME, exercise a pure Nix evaluation, build-user lookup, a fixed-output offline derivation, Cargo and Bun fixtures. Compare resulting paths and exit statuses with the manifest. Repeat the advertised editor-user path if the image supports it.
Run repository testsPin the caller’s checkout independently of the runner repo. Preserve the command, exact test selected, fixture and assertion even when the build succeeds.
Verify host-sensitive activationExercise service units, ownership, users, permissions and host configuration in a disposable NixOS VM. Check what a fresh machine observes after activation and rollback. A container sharing host configuration cannot furnish this evidence.
Fall back to laptop verificationUse a clean worktree at the same commit. Report runner route and environmental differences with the test result. A failed runner preparation has its own disposition.

A drift alarm should compare the three workflow blobs and the local helper and action revisions they load. Record each repository’s visibility, effective runner image, platform and pool owner separately. Byte-identical YAML permits different effective environments. Trigger the comparison on a workflow change and on a bounded scheduled read. Block only promotion of the changed verification route when it differs without an approved exception. Test the alarm with one changed helper and identical workflow files. Workflow parity investigation

Reserve slots by actual provider pool and runner class. Treat macOS as a child of its provider cap and record reservation expiry, admission lag and time to first runnable job. Avoid adding capacity twice where repository aliases schedule against a common owner. Measure R2 cache hit paths divided by eligible requested paths, alongside bytes restored, exported and skipped, elapsed fetch/build time and causes for misses. Count a missing signature, untrusted producer, expired archive and key mismatch separately. Start with paired cold/warm runs at a fixed derivation graph. Permit upload by trusted producers for reusable, verified outputs. A failed export cannot invalidate the workload assertion it followed. Placement and accounting

What the umbrella’s own CI reported

The five permanent warm-export trackers (#35 Nix, #36 OpenCode, #37 code, #38 Zettel and #39 OpenChamber) referenced one first failure. The prebuild pin step invoked a Bash option in sh. PR #40 changed the shell to Bash. Later runs exposed the strict cache export and its worker hostname; those have separate corrections. A green run followed. Keep the first observed failing step, later failure and successful run as separate fields on each tracker. Original run · Shell · Export · Hostname · Green run

The gated #88 run failed its local full-build step. The job annotation records a layer write refused for insufficient scope. Publication legs that were skipped supply no information about their own push grants. Export mode min had already been tried. The exact denied object and the grant that would authorize it remain unestablished. A follow-up diagnosis needs the failed registry operation, target repository and layer ownership without collecting credential values. Apply the narrowest change only after the owning operator confirms the missing grant. Tracker · Failed job · Export change

Convergence across the forks

In the November 23 historical sample, twelve reporting issues itemized 118 failed target attempts over 102 distinct forks and eleven distinct source SHAs. The classifications were 100 failures from missing workflow scope, 15 rule refusals on two forks and three conflicts on one fork. A thirteenth failed workflow could not post its usual report. These denominators describe recorded failures; a fleet-wide failure rate also needs successful attempts in the same window. Issue closure time measures triage. The ancestry test measures convergence. Incident trail · Ruleset case · Reporter correction

Give each observation the target repository ID, upstream SHA, attempt and timestamp. A missing workflow permission or rule exemption belongs with its owner; retry after a grant change. A transient network failure gets bounded backoff within the rate budget. A merge conflict requires target-specific review that preserves the fork’s commits. Prove recovery by testing whether the triggering upstream commit is an ancestor of target HEAD. A newer push may cover an earlier failed attempt. Give incomplete traversal and reporting failure distinct outcomes. Keep the public-only fork boundary during every check.

The missing-installation case in umbrella #87 has a decision history in code #6645. Retaining central push and mirror monitoring avoids new grants and accepts recovery latency when the primary path fails. A pilot installation on selected forks could quantify recovery time and privilege cost. Broader installation needs an explicit owner decision on scopes, affected forks, rotation and removal. Retain current coverage until a measured recovery objective justifies a pilot. Verify installs by application identity and target repository. Fork follow-up · Decision record · Mirror monitoring

Membership and release acceptance

At umbrella revision 45ad3e42, the policy and submodule declarations contained 22 unique matching path/repository pairs. The management tiers comprise one FULL member, four FULL-lite members and seventeen umbrella/autocommit members. The member table records the individual purpose and policy. Devcontainer initialization, warm builds, requested permissions and membership have separate consumers. Never infer access or initialization from a gitlink. Compare the policy, declared path/URL and actual mode-160000 tree entry at one commit. Before adding a member, record its purpose, owner, consumers, tier and removal path. When removing it, unwind consumers and indexing policy before removing the gitlink. Keep private member contents outside the public umbrella. Membership policy and per-member ledger · Submodule declarations

A proposed release manifest identifies the intended Fleet source tree, immutable static asset and SHA-256, bootstrap pin, required capabilities and book revision. Require one observation per deployed broker and operator seat, including service identity, generation, observable source revision, probe time and transition receipt. A channel may deliberately lag with a named owner, reason and next probe. Render unknown when a component cannot be reached. The book receipt should include the built chapter set, CLI surface diff, warning count and the Pages deployment revision. Generate pin text from this manifest where possible; make expired or unsupported pins visible in the currentness check. A runtime feature probe remains useful for mixed-version seats. Publish script · Registry deployment · Release follow-up

Stage promotion as publish and verify, change the bootstrap pin, canary a registered generation, exercise cross-seat probes, then verify the book build at the corresponding revision. A rollback selects the preceding registered generation and appends its outcome. Acceptance fixtures include a wrong asset digest, a missing generation directory, a seat without the required verb, a stale documentation build and a pass with a previously declared exception. Report the observed difference for each component so that a single successful canary cannot certify the fleet.

Quota decisions, operator status and service contracts

A decision record that survives a bad reading

Keep the quota contract alongside the pm-stack gatherer, forecast and review jobs. Publish a versioned observation and decision schema that Fleet’s placement adapter can consume. A new independent quota crate would duplicate classification and provider scope. A pool record needs its provider and billing owner, plan or eligible SKU, binding window, reset, observed and gathered times, source revision and quality. A decision records its input IDs, policy revision, exclusions, selected route and next observation. Preserve the distinction between the current reading and the last known valid reading. Admission design · Admission source and fixtures · Stage-three design

ConditionProposed dispatch decision and oracle
Fresh eligible planBurn by earliest binding expiry with OpenAI as final reserve. Permute provider and input order against a fixed clock and verify a stable result. A provider onboarding manifest supplies meter, reset semantics, included routes, owner and classification fixtures.
Stale, absent, retained-after-error or invalid readAttempt a fresh measurement before a dispatch decision. A result no more than 60 minutes old qualifies. Mark a failed measurement unknown, including source and age. Keep already authorized plan capacity available where documented policy permits it. An unknown cannot establish a wall or financial eligibility.
Admission thresholdTest both sides and equality at 100%, and sustained readings at or above 99.5% over the configured evidence interval. Keep unknown ticks and reset boundaries explicit. Record which admission rule fired.
Provider disableRequire below 1% remaining in the binding window plus corroborating plan-limit failures before disabling a provider. A 402 ends the affected attempt with at most one bounded retry. One failed call cannot disable the provider. Preserve the receipt for each decision.
Section riskPreserve shipped section buckets and the pending-wall threshold of 85%. Include contributing capacity and observation quality. Add forecasts with horizon, estimate and error band, measured against later outcomes by section and reset period.
Possible financial overageAdmit only demonstrably included plan work. Keep money-denominated or unclassified routes out of the eligible set. No provider fallback may widen billing permissions.

The Go placement recorder introduced a separate monthly 97% launch guard. A later revision rejects invalid values, treats a sample retained after a failed tick as stale, retries once and can use the latest valid monthly reading with the fallback recorded. When there is no such reading, the recorder returns failure. Preserve provenance for that path and test how its caller handles the result. A monthly launch reserve, a section notification, a forecast margin, admission and provider disable are distinct outcomes. Source changes establish implementation; deployment and route-wide enforcement require their own observations. Go recorder · Unknown-read handling · Pool launch gate · Section notifications

The S3 shadow input at 12:30:19.472 UTC on November 23 moved 14 of 29 pools in the ordering and demoted one using the forecast. Reproduce that input and both rankings, then collect the deployed gatherer SHA, first qualifying tick, coverage and gaps over the required week. S4’s merged selector is default-off and scoped to one pool. After the S3 evidence and owner gate, record the approved pool, exact margin comparison including equality, deployment and rollback flag. Score a separate live week using S2 outcome records. Check existing in-flight work through the transition. Shadow record · S4 implementation · S4 acceptance

The first published review supplied the evidence recorded at S7’s closure. Its reported opendesign counts give 52 true positives, three false positives, zero false negatives and six true negatives. Precision is 52/55, while three of the nine actual negatives were flagged. The reported median absolute wall-time error was 160.3 minutes. To choose a live margin, evaluate on held-out reset windows, include missed useful dispatches and score repeated ticks separately from distinct window outcomes. Preserve the epic’s two-review criterion and its measured rule change or recorded rationale. Prove scheduled execution with a timer fire and matching report invocation. First score · S7 closure · Epic

One operator read with visible gaps

The queue’s work-inspection API already projects readiness, ownership/execution and remote-resource observations with provenance. Reuse its ID and reference resolvers for a unified status reader. Present per-section source, last successful observation, age, errors and visibility. A timeout yields a partial response. It must never turn a missing queue, quota pool or seat into a measured zero. Bind the caller’s scope before computing aggregates. Inspection projection · Projection tests

Status sectionAuthority and test
WorkCount by stored status at one writer watermark. Classify quarantine with its evidence. Follow the event cursor for claim, park, block, handoff, completion and reasons. Test page continuity during a concurrent append.
DeploymentJoin named active generation and binary source to the intended release manifest and book revision. Simulate one unreachable broker and one deliberately deferred service.
Seats and shortlistJoin enrolled principal, capabilities, last seen and shortlist observation time. Record age of oldest ready entry and the proportion already dispositioned on handout. An offline seat can have unknown depth.
DispatchGroup reservations and provider jobs by dispatch, attempt and job to avoid double counting. Distinguish accepted submission, setup failure and verified workload result.
Quota and channelsShow per-window wall, forecast, reading age and decision separately. For each channel leg, name its dependency and last successful semantic probe.

A 48-hour stall sweep uses the last substantive transition. Heartbeats, observer reads and repair dry runs do not advance it. Report task ID, elapsed time, unresolved native prerequisites, independent body-level gates, holds, owner and next observable event. Future condition-park deadlines are a separate disposition. Test a case where heartbeats continue for 49 hours and a due dependency with a surviving manual gate. A status listing is read-only; ownership and any mutations remain with the responsible operator.

For cost, collect billing owner, platform/SKU, repository, run, attempt, job ID, unit, observed duration, source and price-rule revision. Attribute a job to a lane/task with an explicit relation. Preserve an unattributed bucket and avoid dividing shared jobs arbitrarily. Where the provider rounds per job to whole minutes, two 31-second jobs and a separate 12-second rerun represent three rounded minutes. Check invoice/accounting evidence separately from observed wall clock. Generate Fleet Reports with source watermarks, schema and visibility. Atlas ingestion upserts idempotently by report and revision; advance the export cursor only after acknowledgement. Replay a failed acknowledgement, verify one matching record, and verify the public reader cannot infer private pool or seat membership from aggregates.

Atlas, ID and mcpx

Atlas. Preserve the ranked-chunk and flag-parity contract of the existing CLI. Extend the typed client and retain its renderer. A cache key includes authorized corpus/scope, index generation, ranking/configuration revision, normalized query, filters and limit. A bounded batch API returns a status and ordering per query. Test a mixed denial, timeout and success and compare single-query bytes with the pinned CLI fixture. Telemetry for a golden set needs approved redaction, opt-in sampling and aggregation independent of search results. An offline libSQL replica copies source pages. Use scope-specific datasets and signed manifests with validity, digest and generation. Keep public corpus as the default offline scope. Verify a denied marker is absent even from the persisted replica. A private offline dataset needs a separately accepted revocation-delay bound. Atlas program · Fleet search source

ID. Twelve members in the inspected 13-member Fleet workspace had library roots; the multicall binary composes them. A public Rust function accepting argv or returning an integer exit code promises less than an independently versioned service interface. Build an external minimal Cargo consumer at pinned versions on applicable platforms, inject synthetic transports and secrets, and reject accidentally enabled server features. Preserve the CLI rendering as a compatibility oracle. Workspace and member sources · ID program

CratesProposed embedding boundary and fixture
fleet-registry, fleet-proxy-protoCapability IDs and typed wire frames. Test old and unknown IDs, incompatible or truncated frames, size ceiling and deadline. An advertised capability still requires authorization.
fleet-config, fleet-secretsExplicit settings and injected secret sources. Test precedence with isolated paths and that a denied read stays denied through fallback.
fleet-queueExpose typed leased work operations alongside existing work/placement modules. Use an injected provider, recorded clock and ambiguous submission fixture. Keep broker features optional for remote consumers.
fleet-dispatch, fleet-dispatch-testDistinguish pm orchestration from umbrella verification. Return typed request handles and observations. Cover a successful provider submission followed by lost writeback.
fleet-bridge, fleet-agentReuse contextual execution and the agent’s injectable World. Add typed send/read/ack and intake results. Test acknowledgement replay, no-work, denied and timeout outcomes.
fleet-laptop-agent, fleet-proxyReuse the transport ladder and existing-stream round trip with explicit acquisition and deadlines. An ambiguous receipt cannot safely trigger a duplicate effect on the next leg. Check feature and OS requirements.
fleet-search, fleetExtract the query interface below CLI parsing and retain the binary as the parity oracle. Test the actual consumer lockfile, enabled features and CLI output against a pinned fixture.

mcpx. Add scoped read-only work status and bounded event listing through the existing gateway if a concrete non-Fleet caller requires them. Use existing bridge and Atlas tools for their own domains. A result cursor belongs in the tool’s argument schema and binds the authenticated principal, scope, filters, watermark and expiry. Enforce server-side row and byte ceilings, including for one oversized row. Exercise truncation, empty pages, cross-principal cursor reuse and mid-page revocation. Defer mutation tools until typed lease fencing, replay behavior and per-operation grants are accepted. Treat run-ID propagation in FDR-0005 as a proposal until an accepted decision supplies its lifecycle. Feed seam requirements into the existing hosted-service review. Run identity decision · Hosted architecture

Deliver the schema and offline fixtures first. Shadow the quota and status joins on read-only evidence. Trial one approved pool and one scoped external reader only after their respective gates pass. Publish the measured outcomes, policy revision, rollback owner and remaining unknowns in the existing Fleet book.
